newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dell aims to boost share of Japan's PC market.
newsitem.headline: Dell aims to boost share of Japan's PC market.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp. is looking to increase sales in Japan at two to three times the growth rate in the overall market, Chairman Michael Dell said Tuesday.
"If the market is growing by 20 percent, we would like to grow by 40 to 60 percent," Dell told Reuters after a luncheon at a Tokyo hotel.

He also said the company, one of the world's largest PC makers, will boost its staff in Japan by twofold or threefold in the next three to four years. The company currently employs about 250 at its Japanese unit.
Dell Computer sold 133,000 PCs in 1996 in Japan, accounting for 2 percent of the market, according to the research firm IDC Japan Ltd.
NEC Corp., Japan's top PC maker, shipped 2.6 million units, taking 33 percent of the domestic market, IDC Japan said.

In a move to boost sales in Japan, Dell Tuesday started an on-line commerce service on the Internet for Japanese customers. Dell started the Internet shopping service in the United States in last July, and its sales have exceeded $1 million per day, the company says.

Dell said there is a transition in buying patterns among PC users, in which more users are buying directly from a manufacturer rather than a retailer. A spokesman said Dell expects half of the company's total sales eventually will come from the Internet.
